verdict.rationale: Kick documents user-created rules that 'run automatically every time a matching transaction syncs', alongside AI categorization that runs on sync and is logged under Kick agents, so event-triggered background automation exists. It is limited to transaction-handling rules. The broader MCP/CLI workflow claims depend on an external assistant acting 'with your approval', not on autonomous scheduled jobs. Missing for 10: time-based or recurring scheduled automations, a general workflow/automation builder beyond categorization rules, documented autonomous execution of MCP/CLI workflows, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Once a rule is created, it runs automatically every time a matching transaction syncs.
Rules override AI categorization and run automatically whenever a matching transaction syncs.
automated categorization, transfer matching, and other AI actions are logged under the relevant Kick agent
